properties.displayName: LLMD-001 Direct prompt injection phrasing in user prompt
properties.description:
A user prompt contains well-known instruction-override phrasing ("ignore all previous
instructions", "you are now unrestricted", Hungarian "felejtsd el a korábbi utasításokat").
Keyword matching only catches unsophisticated attempts; pair it with LLMD-003 (canary)
to learn whether an attempt actually succeeded.
properties.query:
let injection = @"(?i)\b(ignore|disregard|forget|override)\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(previous|prior|above|earlier|preceding|system)\b[^.\n]{0,20}\b(instructions?|prompts?|rules|directions|guidelines)\b|\bnew instructions?\s*:|\byou are now\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(unrestricted|unfiltered|uncensored)\b|(felejtsd el|hagyd figyelmen k[ií]v[üu]l|ne vedd figyelembe)[^.\n]{0,30}(kor[áa]bbi|el[őo]z[őo]|fenti|eddigi)[^.\n]{0,15}utas[íi]t[áa]s";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "prompt"
| where prompt matches regex injection
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, app_name, model,
          MatchedPhrase = extract(injection, 0, prompt), prompt

properties.displayName: LLMD-002 Instructions aimed at the model inside retrieved content
properties.description:
A chunk returned by the retriever contains text addressed to the AI (instruction-override
phrasing, "note to the AI assistant", templated image URLs). This means a poisoned document
is in the index and is being served into model context. It fires whether or not the model
obeyed; LLMD-007 tells you if it did. Triage starts with doc_id and doc_source: who uploaded it.
properties.query:
let injection = @"(?i)\b(ignore|disregard|forget|override)\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(previous|prior|above|earlier|preceding|system)\b[^.\n]{0,20}\b(instructions?|prompts?|rules|directions|guidelines)\b|\bnew instructions?\s*:|\byou are now\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(unrestricted|unfiltered|uncensored)\b|(felejtsd el|hagyd figyelmen k[ií]v[üu]l|ne vedd figyelembe)[^.\n]{0,30}(kor[áa]bbi|el[őo]z[őo]|fenti|eddigi)[^.\n]{0,15}utas[íi]t[áa]s";
let addressed_to_model = @"(?i)\b(note|message|instructions?) (to|for) the (ai|assistant|ai assistant|llm|model)\b|\bassistant instructions\s*:|\b(ai|llm) (assistant|agent)\s*:|!\[[^\]]*\]\(https?://[^)\s]*\{[^}]*\}";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "retrieval"
| where chunk_text matches regex injection or chunk_text matches regex addressed_to_model
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Retrievals = count(), Prompts = make_set(request_id, 10)
    by session_id, user_id, src_ip, doc_id, doc_source, doc_title
| extend TimeGenerated = FirstSeen

properties.displayName: LLMD-003 System prompt canary token in model output
properties.description:
The application plants a unique canary string in its system prompt (here: sp-canary-<16 hex>).
The string has no business reason to appear in any output, so a hit is a confirmed system
prompt leak regardless of how the attacker phrased the request. This is the highest-precision
rule in the pack. Rotate the canary per deployment and keep the pattern in sync.
properties.query:
let canary = @"sp-canary-[0-9a-f]{16}";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type in ("completion", "tool_call")
| extend Output = iff(event_type == "completion", completion, tool_args)
| where Output matches regex canary
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, event_type, tool_name,
          Canary = extract(canary, 0, Output), Output

properties.displayName: LLMD-004 Credentials or financial identifiers in model output or tool arguments
properties.description:
A completion, or the arguments of a tool call, contains a secret or financial identifier:
AWS access keys, a secret next to a 40 character key, PEM private keys, GitHub and Slack
tokens, Hungarian IBANs. Checking tool arguments matters: in agentic exfiltration the secret
leaves through send_email or http_get and never shows up in the chat answer.
Pattern matching is defeated by reformatting (see docs/coverage.md, evade-spaced-secret).

properties.displayName: LLMD-005 Auto-loading image with query string to external host in model output
properties.description:
The model emitted a markdown image or HTML img tag that points to a non-corporate host and
carries a query string. Chat clients that render markdown fetch the image without a click, so
whatever is in the query string (often conversation content) reaches the attacker's server.
Clickable links are deliberately out of scope here because they are too common in normal
answers; see docs/coverage.md.
properties.query:
let corporate_domain = "acme-freight.hu";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "completion"
| where completion contains "](http" or completion contains "<img"
| extend ImageUrls = extract_all(@"(?:!\[[^\]]*\]\(|<img[^>]+src=[""']?)(https?://[^)\s""'>]+)", completion)
| mv-expand ImageUrl = ImageUrls to typeof(string)
| extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(ImageUrl).Host)), Query = tostring(parse_url(ImageUrl)["Query Parameters"])
| where ImageUrl contains "?"
// Exact match or a true subdomain; "has" or "contains" would accept acme-freight.hu.evil.com
| where not(Host == corporate_domain or Host endswith strcat(".", corporate_domain))
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, Host, ImageUrl, Query, completion

properties.displayName: LLMD-006 Side-effecting agent tool aimed at an external destination
properties.description:
The assistant called a tool that moves data out (send_email, http_get) with a target outside
the corporate domain and the HTTP allowlist. An agent that can email arbitrary recipients is
an exfiltration channel the moment it reads attacker-controlled text. Tune the two lists to
your environment; anything allowlisted is a blind spot (see evade-allowlisted-exfil).
properties.query:
let corporate_domain = "acme-freight.hu";
let http_allowlist = dynamic(["learn.microsoft.com", "github.com"]);
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_name in ("send_email", "http_get")
| extend Target = tolower(tool_target)
| where not(Target == corporate_domain or Target endswith strcat(".", corporate_domain))
| where not(tool_name == "http_get" and Target in (http_allowlist))
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, tool_name, Target, tool_status, tool_args

properties.displayName: LLMD-007 Egress tool call shortly after externally sourced content entered context
properties.description:
Correlation of LLMD-006 with retrieval: in the same session, a document that did not come from
the internal wiki was pulled into context, and within 10 minutes the agent sent data to an
external destination. This is the shape of a successful indirect prompt injection: the user
asked an ordinary question and the agent acted on instructions from the document.

properties.displayName: LLMD-008 Burst of agent tool calls in one session
properties.description:
Ten or more tool calls in a single session within five minutes. Normal assistant turns use zero
to two tools; an agent looping over the document store, probing paths or retrying denied calls
looks different. Denied calls are surfaced separately because path traversal attempts show up
as denials.

properties.displayName: LLMD-009 Token consumption spike per identity
properties.description:
One identity consumed more than 50 000 tokens within a one hour activity window. Typical
cause: a leaked API key or service credential used to run unrelated workloads on your bill
(cost harvesting), or a scripted denial-of-wallet. The fixed threshold is a starting point;
in production replace it with a per-user baseline (for example series_decompose_anomalies over
14 days). Abuse spread thinly under the threshold is not caught (evade-slow-consumption).
properties.query:
let threshold = 50000;
let trigger_window = 1h;  // see LLMD-008: dedupe across overlapping runs
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "completion"
| sort by user_id asc, TimeGenerated asc
| extend Window = row_window_session(TimeGenerated, 1h, 30m, user_id != prev(user_id))
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated), LastRequest = max(TimeGenerated), Tokens = sum(input_tokens + output_tokens), Requests = count(),
            Sessions = make_set(session_id, 20), SourceIps = make_set(src_ip, 10)
    by user_id, Window
| where Tokens > threshold and LastRequest > ago(trigger_window)
| project-away Window

properties.displayName: LLMD-010 Repeated guardrail blocks from one identity
properties.description:
Three or more prompts from the same user blocked by the input guardrail within ten minutes.
A single block is noise (curiosity, a copy-pasted meme); a series is someone iterating on a
jailbreak. Works with any guardrail that logs its decisions, for example Azure AI Content
Safety Prompt Shields or Llama Prompt Guard, as long as the block becomes a guardrail event.
properties.query:
let threshold = 3;
let trigger_window = 10m;  // see LLMD-008: dedupe across overlapping runs
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "guardrail" and guardrail_action == "block"
| sort by user_id asc, TimeGenerated asc
| extend Window = row_window_session(TimeGenerated, 10m, 10m, user_id != prev(user_id))
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated), LastBlock = max(TimeGenerated), Blocks = count(),
            Rules = make_set(guardrail_rule), SamplePrompts = make_list(prompt, 5),
            Sessions = make_set(session_id), SourceIps = make_set(src_ip)
    by user_id, Window
| where Blocks >= threshold and LastBlock > ago(trigger_window)
| extend src_ip = tostring(SourceIps[0])
| project-away Window

properties.displayName: LLMD-011 Obfuscated content in user prompt (base64, Unicode tags, zero-width)
properties.description:
The prompt carries content a human reviewer would not read directly: a long base64 blob,
invisible Unicode tag characters (U+E0000 to U+E007F, used for "ASCII smuggling"), or runs of
zero-width characters. The query decodes the payload so the analyst sees what was hidden.
properties.query:
let b64 = @"[A-Za-z0-9+/]{60,}={0,2}";
let unicode_tags = @"[\x{E0000}-\x{E007F}]";
let zero_width = @"[\x{200B}-\x{200D}\x{2060}\x{FEFF}]{3,}";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "prompt"
// Real base64 of text mixes upper and lower case; hex digests (SHA-256, commit IDs) do not.
| extend B64Candidate = extract(b64, 0, prompt)
| extend IsB64 = B64Candidate matches regex "[A-Z]" and B64Candidate matches regex "[a-z]"
| extend Technique = case(prompt matches regex unicode_tags, "unicode_tag_smuggling",
                          IsB64, "base64_blob",
                          prompt matches regex zero_width, "zero_width_chars", "")
| where isnotempty(Technique)
| extend Codepoints = unicode_codepoints_from_string(prompt)
| mv-apply Cp = Codepoints to typeof(long) on (
      where Cp between (917504 .. 917631)
      | summarize Hidden = make_list(Cp - 917504))
| extend DecodedPayload = case(Technique == "unicode_tag_smuggling", unicode_codepoints_to_string(Hidden),
                               Technique == "base64_blob", base64_decode_tostring(B64Candidate), "")
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, Technique, DecodedPayload, prompt

properties.description:
The user asks the assistant to repeat, print or reveal its instructions. Low severity on its
own: people are curious. Escalate when the same session also hits LLMD-003 (the canary leaked)
or the user hits LLMD-001 or LLMD-010.
properties.query:
let extraction = @"(?i)\b(repeat|print|reveal|show|output|display|dump)\b[^.\n]{0,25}\b(system prompt|instructions|the text above|everything above|initial prompt|hidden prompt)\b|\bwhat (are|were) your (original |initial |system |hidden )?(instructions|rules|prompt)\b|\brepeat the (text|words) above\b";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "prompt"
| where prompt matches regex extraction
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, MatchedPhrase = extract(extraction, 0, prompt), prompt
